title: Baked Potato, Peel Not Eaten, with Sour Cream

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato without the skin, served with sour cream, is a classic dish in Russian cuisine. The potato is boiled, then baked until a golden crust forms, and finally topped with creamy, tangy sour cream that accentuates its natural flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes were introduced to Europe from South America in the 16th century.
In Russia, baked potatoes are often served as "draniki" or potato croquettes.
The sour cream traditionally used is made from cream of pasture‑fed cows.
Potatoes contain more than 20 vitamins and minerals, including vitamin C, potassium, and vitamin B6.
Baking without the peel makes the dish easier to digest, especially for children and people with stomach sensitivities.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide lasting satiety thanks to slowly digestible starches.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Probiotic effect of sour cream
items.content: Sour cream contains live lactic‑acid bacteria that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When used in moderate amounts, sour cream keeps the dish relatively low‑fat.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk allergy may react to sour cream.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes can raise blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the sour cream is salted, the dish can become a source of excess sodium.

items.title: Thermal processing
items.content: Over‑baking may produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the baked potato hot, drizzled with sour cream. Optional toppings include chopped green onion, dill, or garlic for extra aroma. The dish can be eaten with a fork or spoon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked potato keeps in the refrigerator for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Add sour cream just before serving to preserve its flavor.
